extracted.intended_audience: olympiad contestants, coaches, and contest graders (USAMO/IMO and national olympiads)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines for scoring single mathematical olympiad proofs using the 0–7 scale, intended to direct graders and inform contestants/coaches about how solutions earn or lose points.

rubrics_metrics.name: Score 7
rubrics_metrics.description: Complete, correct solution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Minor presentational issues only. Award a full 7 when the solution is essentially flawless mathematically; only small presentational blemishes (style, notation) may exist.

rubrics_metrics.name: Score 6
rubrics_metrics.description: Essentially complete; small gap easily filled by the grader.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used for solutions that look essentially correct but have a small gap that a grader can fill without reconstructing the whole argument.

rubrics_metrics.name: Score 5
rubrics_metrics.description: Major progress; correct main idea but one substantive step missing or hand-waved.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicates the key idea is present and correct but a substantive step is omitted or only hand-waved; not just minor algebra or presentational slips.

rubrics_metrics.name: Score 4
rubrics_metrics.description: Substantial progress; correct overall framework but key step incomplete.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The overall framework is right and significant work has been done, but an essential step remains incomplete or incorrectly justified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Score 3
rubrics_metrics.description: Several useful observations but no path to a complete proof.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contains multiple correct or promising ideas but lacks the central insight or connection to reach a full solution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Score 2
rubrics_metrics.description: A few correct ideas but missing the central insight.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Shows some understanding and minor progress, but the central idea needed to solve the problem is absent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Score 1
rubrics_metrics.description: One non-trivial observation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only a single meaningful insight or step is present; not enough to build significantly toward a solution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Score 0
rubrics_metrics.description: Nothing of value, or contains a fatal incorrect claim.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Either no useful mathematical content or contains a fundamental/irreparable error that defeats the solution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Two-track grading principle
rubrics_metrics.description: Each solution is approached either from a 7 going down or from a 0 going up.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: From 7 going down: assume a complete solution and deduct for errors — used when the solution looks essentially correct. From 0 going up: assume nothing and add for ideas — used when the solution lacks the key insight. Note: most middle-range scores (3–5) are not awarded by linearly combining small partial credits; a solution typically either has the key idea (7→ track) or doesn’t (0→ track).

rubrics_metrics.name: Gap of Death / rarity of middle scores
rubrics_metrics.description: Middle scores are rare on very hard problems — solutions are often either solved or unsolved.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Putnam example: uses 0,1,2,8,9,10 with middle scores 3–7 essentially never awarded. USAMO allows a wider middle range but follows the same philosophy: either solved (high score) or not (low score).

rubrics_metrics.name: Deductions from a 7
rubrics_metrics.description: Guideline list of typical point deductions applied to an otherwise complete solution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance:
-1 for an algebra/arithmetic slip that doesn't affect the argument.
-1 for missing one easy case.
-1 for unproved "WLOG" that has a non-trivial reduction.
-2 for skipping a step that genuinely requires work.
0 if the solution is correct but written illegibly.
Use these as a menu of common deductions when starting from a 7 and reducing for faults.

rubrics_metrics.name: Additions from a 0
rubrics_metrics.description: Guideline list of typical partial-credit increments when building up from nothing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance:
+1 for a correct restatement showing understanding of the problem.
+1 for a non-trivial necessary condition derived.
+1 for a worked-out small case providing insight.
+2 for the central lemma but missing the conclusion.
Use these to award credit when the solution lacks the key idea but contains useful correct components.

rubrics_metrics.name: Logical completeness
rubrics_metrics.description: Every step justified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Grader expects justification for each inferential step; unstated or unjustified steps cause deductions.

rubrics_metrics.name: No gaps (no hidden work)
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid 'obvious' / 'clearly' / 'WLOG' hiding real work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Statements like 'it is obvious' or omitted arguments are penalized if they hide nontrivial work; 'WLOG' must be justified when the reduction is nontrivial.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correct quantifier handling
rubrics_metrics.description: Every variable's scope and quantifiers are handled correctly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure universal/existential quantifiers and dependencies are made explicit; ambiguous quantification leads to deductions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Case exhaustiveness
rubrics_metrics.description: All cases must be disjoint and complete.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When solving by cases, show the cases cover all possibilities and are pairwise disjoint (or properly handled); missing or overlapping cases are penalized.

rubrics_metrics.name: The right key insight
rubrics_metrics.description: Presence of the problem's intended trick or a valid alternative central idea.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Grading hinges on whether the solver has the central idea (or an equally powerful alternative). Without the key insight, middle-high scores are not awarded.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarity
rubrics_metrics.description: Grader should not have to reconstruct the argument.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clear exposition—well-organized, readable, and logically flowing proofs—helps secure higher scores; solutions requiring reconstruction are docked.

rubrics_metrics.name: Verification for 'find all' problems
rubrics_metrics.description: Show that the listed solutions work and prove there are no others.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Two-fold obligation: (1) verify proposed solutions satisfy the problem, and (2) provide a proof of completeness (no other solutions exist). Skipping verification is explicitly docked.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dock: skipping verification
rubrics_metrics.description: Penalty for failing to check/verify candidate solutions in 'find all' problems.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Omitting the verification step leads to deductions even if the derived candidates look plausible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dock: unjustified 'WLOG'
rubrics_metrics.description: Penalty for asserting 'WLOG' without checking the symmetry holds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the reduction claimed by 'WLOG' is non-trivial, the reduction must be shown; otherwise apply deductions (often -1).

rubrics_metrics.name: Dock: 'It is easy to see' without justification
rubrics_metrics.description: Penalty for asserting things are obvious when they are not.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Phrases claiming obviousness that skip substantive argument are penalized; provide the missing justification or a reference at contest-appropriate level.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dock: missing base case in induction
rubrics_metrics.description: Penalty for inductive arguments that omit an explicit base case.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Induction must include a clear base case and inductive step; omission leads to deductions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dock: unjustified continuity/convergence claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Penalty in analysis problems for asserting continuity/convergence without proof.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Continuity or limit arguments must be justified; bare assertions are not acceptable at olympiad level.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dock: using high-level theorems without restatement
rubrics_metrics.description: Penalty for invoking a known theorem above the contest level without restating it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If using a theorem beyond typical contest knowledge, restate or prove it; simply citing 'by theorem X' without justification is penalized.
